subject: mathematics
question_text: If α, β are the solutions of the equation a cosθ + b sinθ = c, where a, b, c ∈ R, then show that (i) sinα + sinβ = 2bc/(a²+b²), (ii) sinα · sinβ = (c²−a²)/(a²+b²).

mark_split.label: Read off the sum and product

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name each move in order, and say which general solution formula you would use.

steps.label: Isolate and square
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Move the sine term across so only the cosine is on one side, then square — which turns cos²θ into 1 − sin²θ and leaves everything in sine.
lines: Given a cosθ + b sinθ = c
⇒ a²(1 − sin²θ) = c² + b² sin²θ − 2bc sinθ
⇒ a² − a² sin²θ = c² + b² sin²θ − 2bc sinθ

recall.must_convey: That the cosine is isolated and both sides squared, so cos²θ becomes 1 − sin²θ and the equation is in sine alone.
accept: isolate a cos theta then square both sides so cos squared becomes one minus sin squared
move the sine across and square to get everything in sine
a cos theta ni veru chesi square cheste sine lo vasthundi

steps.why: Squaring is what removes the cosine, and it is legitimate here because the roots are being characterised, not found — any extraneous root introduced would still satisfy the squared equation.
common_mistakes: Squaring the equation as it stands, leaving a cross term in sinθcosθ.
Forgetting the middle term of (c − b sinθ)².

steps.label: Collect into a quadratic
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Bring everything to one side. The sin²θ terms combine to (a²+b²), which is where the denominator of both answers comes from.
lines: Transposing all terms to one side:
⇒ a² sin²θ + b² sin²θ − 2bc sinθ + c² − a² = 0

recall.must_convey: That the terms collect into (a²+b²)sin²θ − 2bc sinθ + (c²−a²) = 0.
accept: collect everything to get a squared plus b squared sin squared minus two b c sin plus c squared minus a squared equals zero
transpose and combine the sin squared terms
the quadratic is a squared plus b squared sin squared minus two bc sin plus c squared minus a squared
anni okate vaipuki teesi collect cheyyali

steps.why: α and β are the two solutions, so sinα and sinβ are the two roots of this quadratic — exactly the same logic as the twin, reached by a different route.
common_mistakes: Sign slip on the c² − a² term.
Failing to gather both sin²θ terms.

steps.label: Read off the sum and product
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Sum of roots is −B/A and product is C/A. Both denominators are (a²+b²), and the two minus signs on the sum cancel.
lines: This is a quadratic in sinθ with roots sinα, sinβ.

recall.must_convey: That the sum of roots is 2bc/(a²+b²) and the product is (c²−a²)/(a²+b²).
accept: the sum is minus B over A which is two b c over a squared plus b squared and the product is c squared minus a squared over a squared plus b squared
read the sum and product off the coefficients
sum two b c by a square plus b square and product c square minus a square by a square plus b square
sum of roots and product of roots formulas vaadali
both come straight from the coefficients

steps.why: Neither α nor β is ever found. The whole method is to recognise them as roots and read the two symmetric functions off the coefficients — which is faster and exact.
common_mistakes: Trying to solve for α and β individually.
Keeping the minus on the sum.
